taxonomy:
Below is a rule-based taxonomy of the listed grid logic games, using only features explicitly stated in the provided rules.

---

# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## I. By primary player action

### A. Placement / filling in cells
Games where the main action is to place symbols, numbers, black cells, white cells, or marks into cells.

#### A1. Binary shading / coloring of cells
Cells are painted black / left white, or colored / uncolored.

- **Chained Block** — fill cells black/white to form numbered black “blocks” and chains
- **Choco Banana** — paint cells black
- **Hebi** — place numbers in white squares as snake parts
- **Heyawake** — fill cells, with painted cells constrained by rooms
- **Hitori** — color cells black/white
- **Juosan** — fill every cell with either “—” or “|”
- **Kurodoko** — color cells black
- **Kurotto** — fill/color cells black around circles
- **LITS** — color tetromino cells in each room
- **Norinori** — place black cells in pairs
- **Nurimeizu** — paint cells to make walls / leave white maze path
- **Nurimisaki** — fill cells black/white under “Misaki” constraints
- **Nurikabe** — fill cells black/white
- **Nuritwin** — shade some cells
- **Sto-stone** — fill colored cells / place black cells in rooms
- **Tilepaint** — color tiles black or leave uncolored
- **Usowan** — fill/color cells

#### A2. Number placement in cells
The main action is entering numbers.

- **Fillomino** — fill empty cells with numbers, making same-number polyominoes
- **Makaro** — fill rooms with numbers 1 up to room size
- **Sudoku** — place digits 1–9
- **Ripple Effect** — fill rooms with consecutive numbers
- **Hebi** — also fits here, since snake cells are numbered 1 to 5

#### A3. Shape or symbol placement in cells
The player places non-numeric objects or shape markers.

- **Akari** — place light bulbs
- **Evolomino** — draw squares in cells
- **Shakashaka** — place triangular pieces in cells

---

### B. Partition / region-division games
Games where the main action is drawing borders or dividing the grid into blocks.

- **Double Choco** — divide grid into blocks by drawing lines
- **Five Cells** — divide grid into blocks of five cells
- **Sashigane** — divide grid into L-shaped blocks
- **Shikaku** — divide grid into rectangles

---

### C. Line / path / loop drawing games
Games where the main action is drawing a path, loop, or network.

#### C1. Single-loop through cells
Loop goes through cell centers.

- **Dotchi-Loop**
- **Masyu**
- **Mid-loop**
- **Moon-or-Sun**
- **Nagareru**
- **Suraromu**
- **Yajilin** — draw a single loop that avoids black and clue cells

#### C2. Single-loop on lattice edges / around cells
Loop is formed by connecting dots or surrounding cells.

- **Slitherlink** — connect adjacent dots to make a single loop

#### C3. Non-loop path connection
Paths connect endpoints or obey movement constraints, but are not necessarily one loop.

- **Numberlink** — connect equal numbers
- **Pencils** — draw lines from pencil tips
- **Satogaeri** — move circles by straight tracks
- **Yosenabe** — move circles into gray areas by straight arrows

#### C4. Network / connection without generic path cells
- **Hashiwokakero** — connect numbered islands with bridges

---

### D. Entry from a given list / word-number packing
The content to place is selected from a supplied set.

- **Nansuke** — fill blank cells with numbers from a list

---

## II. By structural object being formed

### A. Loop-forming puzzles
Explicit requirement of a single loop.

- **Dotchi-Loop**
- **Masyu**
- **Mid-loop**
- **Moon-or-Sun**
- **Nagareru**
- **Slitherlink**
- **Suraromu**
- **Yajilin**

### B. Path-connection puzzles
Create paths, routes, or tracks, but not necessarily one loop.

- **Numberlink**
- **Pencils**
- **Satogaeri**
- **Yosenabe**

### C. Bridge/network puzzles
- **Hashiwokakero**

### D. Region-formation / partition puzzles
- **Double Choco**
- **Five Cells**
- **Fillomino**
- **Sashigane**
- **Shikaku**

### E. Shaded-region topology puzzles
The core object is a black/white configuration with connectivity and shape constraints.

- **Chained Block**
- **Choco Banana**
- **Heyawake**
- **Hitori**
- **Kurodoko**
- **Kurotto**
- **LITS**
- **Norinori**
- **Nurimeizu**
- **Nurimisaki**
- **Nurikabe**
- **Nuritwin**
- **Sto-stone**
- **Tilepaint**
- **Usowan**
- **Yajilin** — also includes black cells in addition to loop

### F. Number-pattern / Latin-style puzzles
- **Sudoku**
- **Makaro**
- **Ripple Effect**

### G. Object-evolution / growth puzzles
- **Evolomino** — blocks along arrows grow by one square
- **Hebi** — snakes are sequential chains 1→5

### H. Rectangle/square completion or avoidance puzzles
- **Choco Banana** — black connected cells form rectangles/squares; white connected cells must not
- **Shakashaka** — uncovered white regions form rectangles/squares
- **Shikaku** — divide into rectangles

---

## III. By role of bold-line rooms or regions

### A. Games explicitly using pre-divided rooms/areas as central constraints
- **Dotchi-Loop**
- **Double Choco**
- **Heyawake**
- **Juosan** (“Territories”)
- **LITS**
- **Makaro**
- **Moon-or-Sun**
- **Nurimeizu** (“Rooms”)
- **Nuritwin** (outlined regions)
- **Ripple Effect** (“Rooms”)
- **Sto-stone** (“Rooms”)
- **Tilepaint** (“Tiles”)
- **Usowan** (rectangles bordered by bold lines)
- **Satogaeri** (“Countries”)
- **Norinori** (areas surrounded by bold lines)

### B. Games not primarily based on pre-divided rooms
- **Akari**
- **Chained Block**
- **Choco Banana**
- **Evolomino**
- **Five Cells**
- **Fillomino**
- **Hashiwokakero**
- **Hebi**
- **Hitori**
- **Kurodoko**
- **Kurotto**
- **Masyu**
- **Nagareru**
- **Nansuke**
- **Nurimisaki**
- **Mid-loop**
- **Numberlink**
- **Nurikabe**
- **Pencils**
- **Sashigane**
- **Shakashaka**
- **Shikaku**
- **Slitherlink**
- **Sudoku**
- **Suraromu**
- **Yajilin**
- **Yosenabe**

---

## IV. By clue type

### A. Number clues in cells
- **Akari**
- **Chained Block**
- **Choco Banana**
- **Five Cells**
- **Fillomino**
- **Hebi** (black clue cells with arrows and numbers)
- **Heyawake**
- **Hitori**
- **Juosan**
- **Kurodoko**
- **Makaro**
- **Nurikabe**
- **Nuritwin**
- **Pencils**
- **Ripple Effect**
- **Shakashaka**
- **Shikaku**
- **Slitherlink**
- **Sto-stone**
- **Sudoku**
- **Tilepaint**
- **Usowan**
- **Yajilin**
- **Yosenabe**

### B. Number clues in circles / islands
- **Hashiwokakero** — numbered islands
- **Kurotto** — numbers in circles
- **Masyu** — black/white circles, though not numeric
- **Mid-loop** — black circles, non-numeric
- **Nurimisaki** — numbers in circles
- **Sashigane** — numbers in open circles
- **Satogaeri** — numbers in circles
- **Suraromu** — open numbered circle plus numbers in black cells

### C. Arrow clues
- **Evolomino** — pre-drawn arrows hosting squares and growth order
- **Hebi** — arrows in black cells indicate nearest snake part
- **Makaro** — black cells with arrows point to local maximum
- **Nagareru** — black arrow cells and wind arrows
- **Sashigane** — arrows indicate block ends toward knees
- **Yajilin** — arrow-number clues
- **Yosenabe** — arrows are used to show circle movement in solution

### D. Circle-color clues
- **Dotchi-Loop** — white circles and black circles
- **Masyu** — white and black circles
- **Moon-or-Sun** — moon cells and sun cells
- **Nurimeizu** — circle and triangle markers
- **Nurimisaki** — circle cells
- **Mid-loop** — black circles

### E. External clue list
- **Nansuke** — uses numbers in a list below the grid

---

## V. By dominant geometric constraint

### A. Connectivity of white cells required
- **Heyawake**
- **Hitori**
- **Kurodoko**
- **Nurimisaki**
- **Usowan**

### B. Connectivity of black/shaded cells required
- **LITS**
- **Nurikabe**
- **Nuritwin** — all shaded cells connected
- **Sto-stone** — local black runs in rooms, then dropped configuration fills bottom half
- **Chained Block** — all blocks must belong to chains via corner contact

### C. Black/shaded cells may not touch orthogonally
- **Heyawake**
- **Hitori**
- **Kurodoko**
- **Usowan**
- **Yajilin**

### D. No 2×2 all-black / all-shaded / large square constraints
- **LITS** — colored squares cannot form 2×2 or larger squares
- **Nurimeizu** — black and white cells cannot cover 2×2 or larger squares
- **Nurimisaki** — neither black nor white cells can make 2×2 or larger
- **Nurikabe** — black cells cannot be 2×2 or larger
- **Nuritwin** — no 2×2 entirely shaded

### E. Rectangle / square formation constraints
- **Choco Banana** — black regions must be rectangles/squares; white regions must not
- **Shakashaka** — remaining white areas must form rectangles/squares
- **Shikaku** — all regions are rectangles

### F. Shape uniqueness / polyform constraints
- **Chained Block** — no chain may contain more than one block of same size and shape up to rotation/mirror
- **Double Choco** — each block contains matching white and gray shapes
- **Evolomino** — successive blocks add one square without rotation/flipping
- **LITS** — same tetromino shape may not touch, even by rotated/reflected form
- **Nuritwin** — two blocks in a region have same number of cells

---

## VI. By movement or displacement theme

### A. Static placement puzzles
Most listed games, including:
**Akari, Chained Block, Choco Banana, Double Choco, Evolomino, Five Cells, Fillomino, Hebi, Heyawake, Hitori, Juosan, Kurodoko, Kurotto, LITS, Makaro, Nansuke, Norinori, Nurimeizu, Nurimisaki, Nurikabe, Nuritwin, Ripple Effect, Sashigane, Shakashaka, Shikaku, Sto-stone, Sudoku, Tilepaint, Usowan**

### B. Explicit movement of objects
- **Satogaeri** — circles move into countries
- **Yosenabe** — circles move into gray areas
- **Sto-stone** — stones are conceptually “dropped” downward
- **Nagareru** — loop direction interacts with wind movement
- **Pencils** — lines emerge from pencil tips as directed extension

---

## VII. By whether all cells must be used by the main structure

### A. Main structure uses all or nearly all cells
- **Fillomino** — all cells filled with numbers
- **Juosan** — all cells filled with marks
- **Makaro** — all empty cells filled
- **Nansuke** — all blank cells filled
- **Sudoku** — every empty cell filled
- **Ripple Effect** — all empty cells filled
- **Shikaku** — whole grid partitioned
- **Five Cells** — whole grid partitioned
- **Sashigane** — whole grid partitioned into Ls

### B. Main structure selects some cells only
- **Akari**
- **Chained Block**
- **Choco Banana**
- **Evolomino**
- **Hebi**
- **Heyawake**
- **Hitori**
- **Kurodoko**
- **Kurotto**
- **LITS**
- **Norinori**
- **Nurimeizu**
- **Nurimisaki**
- **Nurikabe**
- **Nuritwin**
- **Shakashaka**
- **Sto-stone**
- **Tilepaint**
- **Usowan**
- **Yajilin**

### C. Main structure is primarily line-based rather than cell-filling
- **Dotchi-Loop**
- **Hashiwokakero**
- **Masyu**
- **Mid-loop**
- **Moon-or-Sun**
- **Nagareru**
- **Numberlink**
- **Pencils**
- **Satogaeri**
- **Slitherlink**
- **Suraromu**
- **Yosenabe**

---

# Compact classification table

| Game | Primary action | Core structure |
|---|---|---|
| Akari | place objects | bulb illumination |
| Chained Block | shade cells | black blocks/chains |
| Choco Banana | shade cells | rectangular black regions |
| Dotchi-Loop | draw loop | single loop through cells |
| Double Choco | partition | matched white/gray shapes in blocks |
| Evolomino | place squares | growing polyomino sequence |
| Five Cells | partition | 5-cell regions |
| Fillomino | fill numbers | same-number polyominoes |
| Hashiwokakero | draw bridges | connected island network |
| Hebi | place numbers | snakes 1→5 |
| Heyawake | shade cells | room-constrained black/white pattern |
| Hitori | shade cells | duplicate elimination + white connectivity |
| Juosan | fill marks | dash/bar pattern by territories |
| Kurodoko | shade cells | visibility counts |
| Kurotto | shade cells | black-cell sums from circles |
| LITS | shade cells | tetromino per room |
| Masyu | draw loop | loop with black/white circle behavior |
| Nagareru | draw loop | directed loop with wind |
| Nansuke | fill digits | packing list-given numbers |
| Norinori | shade cells | black domino pairs |
| Nurimeizu | shade cells | maze path by room coloring |
| Nurimisaki | shade cells | white promontories |
| Makaro | fill numbers | room numbering with arrow maxima |
| Mid-loop | draw loop | loop through circle midpoints |
| Moon-or-Sun | draw loop | room-by-room moon/sun alternation |
| Numberlink | draw paths | connect equal numbers |
| Nurikabe | shade cells | numbered white islands + black wall |
| Nuritwin | shade cells | two equal-size shaded blocks per region |
| Pencils | draw paths | pencils and lead lines |
| Ripple Effect | fill numbers | room sequences with spacing rule |
| Sashigane | partition | L-shaped regions |
| Satogaeri | move circles | noncrossing relocation tracks |
| Shakashaka | place triangles | white rectangles/squares |
| Shikaku | partition | numbered rectangles |
| Slitherlink | draw loop | edge loop by cell counts |
| Sto-stone | shade cells | room black counts + gravity test |
| Sudoku | fill numbers | 1–9 Latin/block grid |
| Suraromu | draw loop | gate-order loop |
| Tilepaint | shade tiles | tile coloring by line counts |
| Usowan | shade cells | one false clue per room |
| Yajilin | draw loop + shade | loop with arrow black-count clues |
| Yosenabe | move circles | arrows into gray sum areas |
